cases.sentence: Но тут меня кто-то с разгона трахнул головой по ___.
cases.translation: But then someone came at a run and butted me on the back with his head.
cases.explain: «По» meaning 'along / over the surface of' governs the dative, so спина becomes спине.

cases.sentence: Передо мною был некто без ___, без хвоста и без головы.
cases.translation: In front of me stood someone with no legs, no tail and no head.
cases.explain: The preposition «без» always takes the genitive; here the plural genitive of нога is the zero-ending form ног.
With the verb «быть» left out, the thing being identified is the subject of the sentence and stays in the nominative.
«В» answering «куда?» (motion towards) takes the accusative; Петушки is inanimate, so the accusative is identical to the nominative.

cases.translation: You will solve five riddles of mine for me.
cases.explain: Numerals from пять upwards are followed by the genitive plural, so загадка becomes загадок.

cases.translation: Someone hit me on the back with his tail.
cases.explain: The thing used to perform an action — the instrument of the blow — goes into the instrumental with no preposition.

cases.sentence: Твоя паскуда валяется в ___ и виссоне.
cases.translation: Your hussy is sprawled in jasmine and fine linen.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional: в жасмине.

cases.sentence: Папанин, желая спасти ___, вышел в сторону пункта Б2.
cases.translation: Papanin, wishing to rescue Vodopyanov, set out in the direction of point B2.
cases.explain: «Спасти» takes a direct object in the accusative; Водопьянов is animate, so its accusative copies the genitive form Водопьянова.

reading.ru: Чуть только я забылся, кто-то ударил меня хвостом по спине.
reading.question: What interrupts Venichka the moment he starts to drift off?
options: Someone hits him on the back with a tail
The conductor asks for his ticket
reading.correct: Someone hits him on the back with a tail
reading.explain: He is prevented from surrendering to the flow of his thoughts by a blow from a tail.

reading.ru: Я вздрогнул и обернулся: передо мною был некто без ног, без хвоста и без головы.
reading.question: How is the creature described when Venichka first turns round?
options: As someone with no legs, no tail and no head
As a tall man in a railway uniform
As an old woman with a basket
As a boy of about twelve
reading.correct: As someone with no legs, no tail and no head
reading.explain: The joke is that the thing which just struck him with a tail is described as having none.

reading.ru: Но тут меня кто-то с разгона трахнул головой по спине.
reading.question: What happens after Venichka offendedly turns away for the second time?
options: Someone butts him on the back with his head at a run
He is thrown off the train
reading.correct: Someone butts him on the back with his head at a run
reading.explain: The second blow is delivered with a head, again by the being that supposedly has neither head nor legs.

reading.ru: На этот раз – я все-таки решил угадать.
reading.question: Why does Venichka finally decide to try guessing?
options: He fears that otherwise he will be hit on the back with both legs
He is genuinely curious about the answer
He wants to impress the other passengers
He has been promised a drink
reading.correct: He fears that otherwise he will be hit on the back with both legs
reading.explain: He reasons that if he turns away again the creature may well whack him with both legs.

reading.question: Who does the creature announce itself to be?
reading.explain: It introduces itself as the Sphinx before setting its riddles.

reading.ru: И он в этот город тебя не пустит.
reading.question: What does the Sphinx declare about Petushki?
options: That he will not let Venichka into the town
That the town has burned down
That the train no longer stops there
reading.correct: That he will not let Venichka into the town
reading.explain: The Sphinx's whole purpose in the chapter is to bar the way to Petushki.

reading.ru: Вернее, пущу при одном условии: ты разгадаешь мне пять моих загадок.
reading.question: On what condition will the Sphinx let Venichka through?
options: If he hands over his little suitcase
If he pays for a ticket
reading.explain: The single condition named is solving the Sphinx's five riddles.

reading.question: What is Venichka's verdict on the first riddle, about the shock-worker Stakhanov?
options: That it is a bad riddle with a piggish subtext
That it is too easy to bother with
That it is the only fair one of the five
That he has heard it before
reading.correct: That it is a bad riddle with a piggish subtext
reading.explain: He takes offence at the riddle about Stakhanov's trips to the lavatory and refuses to solve it.

reading.question: How does Venichka respond to the second riddle, about the American fleet at Petushki?
options: He refuses it too, calling it a very ugly riddle
He solves it and gives the number 428
He asks the Sphinx to repeat it
He laughs and agrees it is clever
reading.correct: He refuses it too, calling it a very ugly riddle
reading.explain: He apologises but declines, then asks for the third riddle instead.

reading.question: According to the third riddle, what kind of points are there in Petushki?
options: Points A and C but no B
reading.explain: The riddle states that Petushki has no points A and still fewer points C — nothing but points B.

reading.question: In the riddle about Lord Chamberlain, what happened to the plates on the overturned table?
options: They were never on the table
reading.explain: The plates survived while all the dishes on them were ruined.

reading.question: Where does Venichka object that Lord Chamberlain slipped?
options: In the restaurant at Petushki station
In the restaurant at the Kursk station
reading.correct: In the restaurant at Petushki station
reading.explain: He protests that the fall happened in the Petushki restaurant, not at the Kursk station.

reading.ru: А счет оплатил на Курском вокзале.
reading.question: How does the Sphinx answer that objection?
options: The bill was paid at the Kursk station
The bill was never paid at all
The bill was paid in Petushki after all
Lord Chamberlain paid it in London
reading.correct: The bill was paid at the Kursk station
reading.explain: Wherever the fall took place, the Sphinx insists the bill was settled at the Kursk station.

reading.question: What does Venichka call the fourth riddle?
reading.explain: He says it is not a riddle but mockery; the Sphinx replies that it is a riddle all the same.

reading.ru: И оба попали на Курский вокзал.
reading.question: Where do Minin and Pozharsky end up after each takes the other's road?
reading.explain: Having persuaded each other to turn back, both arrive at the Kursk station.

reading.ru: А в Петушки, ха-ха, вообще никто не попадет!..
reading.question: What is the Sphinx's triumphant conclusion to the last riddle?
options: That nobody at all will ever get to Petushki
That only Minin will get to Petushki
That only Pozharsky will get to Petushki
That both of them will get to Petushki
reading.correct: That nobody at all will ever get to Petushki
reading.explain: Whichever road they take, both men end at the Kursk station, so no one reaches Petushki.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the second blow Venichka receives?
sentences: Я обиженно отвернулся от него, чтобы снова забыться.
Но тут меня кто-то с разгона трахнул головой по спине.
Я опять обернулся: передо мною был все тот же некто, без ног, без хвоста и без головы…
highlight.explain: Only the second sentence reports the blow itself, struck with a head at a run.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what the creature did while it waited for Venichka to think?
sentences: Я опустил глаза и задумался.
Он – ждал, пока я додумаюсь, и в ожидании тихо поводил кулачищем у самых моих ноздрей.
Как будто он мне, дураку, сопли вытирал…
highlight.explain: The middle sentence shows it quietly moving its huge fist under his nostrils as it waited.

highlight.question: Which sentence states the condition on which Venichka will be allowed into Petushki?
sentences: Там хуже, чем дочь и язва.
Мне лучше знать, что там.
Но я сказал тебе – не пущу, значит не пущу.
Вернее, пущу при одном условии: ты разгадаешь мне пять моих загадок.
highlight.explain: The last sentence introduces the bargain of the five riddles.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what kind of subtext the first riddle has?
sentences: Это плохая загадка.
Сфинкс, это загадка с поросячьим подтекстом.
Я не буду разгадывать эту плохую загадку.
highlight.explain: The second sentence is the one that names the piggish subtext.

highlight.question: Which sentence asks the Sphinx to move on to the next riddle?
sentences: Я не буду решать и эту загадку, Сфинкс.
Ты меня прости, но я не буду.
Это очень некрасивая загадка.
Давай лучше третью.
highlight.explain: The closing sentence asks for the third riddle instead of the second.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells what the Sphinx did besides laughing?
sentences: Что это был за смех у этого подлеца!
Я ни разу в жизни не слышал такого живодерского смеха!
Да добро бы он только смеялся! – а то ведь он, не переставая смеяться, схватил меня за нос двумя суставами и куда-то потащил…
highlight.explain: The last sentence reports him seizing Venichka by the nose and dragging him off.
